I am applying for Ph.D. programs in applied mathematics and scientific computing for Fall 2027. My research interests are numerical analysis, scientific computing, and stochastic analysis.

I hold a B.Sc. in Mathematics and Applied Mathematics from Tongji University and an M.Phil. in Mathematics from The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen. My undergraduate work concerned wavelet-frame image restoration; my master's thesis studied numerical valuation and multi-factor strategies for Chinese convertible bonds. These projects shaped my path from numerical optimization to stochastic simulation and numerical analysis.

I am currently studying stochastic analysis. My subsequent backend-development work also added programming and implementation experience.

Research Experience

Numerical Valuation and Multi-Factor Strategies for Chinese Convertible Bonds

M.Phil. research · CUHK-Shenzhen · 2023–2024 · Advisor: Prof. Gongqiu Zhang

My master's thesis addresses two connected questions: how to numerically value Chinese convertible bonds with complex contractual provisions, and how to construct and evaluate bond-selection strategies using valuation signals and market factors. The thesis covers simulation-based valuation, empirical pricing studies, and machine-learning-based multi-factor strategies.

  • Simulation-based valuation.Simulated geometric Brownian stock-price paths and incorporated call, put, and conversion-price reset provisions. Used least-squares regression to estimate continuation values within a backward dynamic-programming recursion, and compared global regression with regressions fitted by stock-price region.
  • Empirical pricing and strategy evaluation.Compared model and market prices for ten AAA-rated convertible bonds. Constructed an undervaluation-based selection strategy and used the double-low strategy as a historical backtesting benchmark.
  • Multi-factor modelling.Evaluated factors using information coefficient (IC) analysis and stratified backtesting. Compared linear and polynomial regression, SVM, random forests, XGBoost, LightGBM, and MLP using rolling-window train–test splits, including 7-, 10-, and 20-day training windows.
  • Strategy validation.Constructed multi-factor strategies using SVM and linear regression, and evaluated them in the thesis's 118-trading-day simulation sample with an assumed transaction cost of 0.1%.

The project helped me understand how state variables, regression features, contractual exercise rules, and training windows affect computational results. It also motivated my interest in approximation and error analysis for numerical methods.

Thesis validation results and limitations

Table 4.8 of the master's thesis reports annualized returns of 13.22% for the SVM strategy and 18.62% for linear regression over a 118-trading-day sample in February–July 2023, assuming a transaction cost of 0.1%. These are historical simulation results under specific sample and modelling choices, rather than live-trading performance. The thesis identifies the limited data sample and overfitting in some nonlinear models as limitations.

Image Restoration and Numerical Optimization with Wavelet Frames

Undergraduate thesis · Tongji University · Advisor: Jae Kyu Choi

Studied analysis-based, synthesis-based, and balanced wavelet-frame formulations for image reconstruction, and the application of the alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) to the analysis-based model. My focus was on understanding the formulations and their numerical solution.

Thesis: Image Restoration, a Wavelet Frame Based Approach and Beyond
